questions.question_text: Which of the following laboratory results would be suggestive of Wilson's disease?

options.text: Low blood ceruloplasmin and low urinary copper.
Low blood ceruloplasmin and high urinary copper.
High blood ceruloplasmin and low urinary copper.
High blood ceruloplasmin and high urinary copper.
High blood ceruloplasmin and normal urinary copper.

correct_answer.text: Low blood ceruloplasmin and high urinary copper.

correct_answers.text: Low blood ceruloplasmin and high urinary copper.

questions.explanation: Low blood ceruloplasmin and high urinary copper content aid in the diagnosis of Wilson’s disease

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about delirium is true?

options.text: Disorientation to person, place, or time must be present to meet DSM-5 criteria for delirium.
The hallmark of delirium is impaired attention.
Change in psychomotor activity is an uncommon clinical manifestation of delirium.
Delirium has a lower degree of personality disorganization and clouding of consciousness compared with mild or major neurocognitive disorder.
Delirium generally takes weeks to months to resolve.

correct_answer.text: The hallmark of delirium is impaired attention.

correct_answers.text: The hallmark of delirium is impaired attention.

questions.explanation: Delirium is a state of altered consciousness and cognition, usually of acute onset (hours or days) and brief duration (days or weeks). The hallmark of delirium is impaired attention. DSM-5 criteria require a disturbance in attention and awareness, as well as an additional disturbance in cognition; however, many persons with delirium remain oriented to person, place, and time but demonstrate impairment on tests of sustained attention. Reduced or increased psychomotor activity is common. Delirium has a greater degree of personality disorganization and clouding of consciousness than mild or major neurocognitive disorder.

questions.question_text: What cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings would you expect in Alzheimer's disease?

options.text: Normal.
High b-amyloid 42 and low tau and phosphorylated tau.
Low b-amyloid 42 and high tau and phosphorylated tau.
Low b-amyloid 42 and low tau and phosphorylated tau.
High b-amyloid 42 and high tau and phosphorylated tau.

correct_answer.text: Low b-amyloid 42 and high tau and phosphorylated tau.

correct_answers.text: Low b-amyloid 42 and high tau and phosphorylated tau.

questions.explanation: The finding of low CSF b-amyloid42 and high total tau and phosphorylated tau is confirmatory of a suspected diagnosis of major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to Alzheimer’s disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurocognitive disorders is associated with rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder?

options.text: Alzheimer's disease.
Frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
Lewy body disease.
Cerebrovascular disease.
Neurocognitive disorder associated with traumatic brain injury.

correct_answer.text: Lewy body disease.

correct_answers.text: Lewy body disease.

questions.explanation: A distinctive clinical feature of Lewy body disease is that an REM sleep behavior disorder is a frequent concomitant and often precedes cognitive symptoms. Other characteristic clinical features that may aid in the diagnosis include the sudden onset of visual hallucinations, which frequently remit and reoccur. There are marked fluctuations in sensorium, with episodes of confusion lasting days or weeks followed by relative clarity for equal periods of time. Mild parkinsonism occurs early on. Functional brain imaging frequently shows low blood flow or low metabolic activity in the occipital lobes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the diagnosis of language-variant frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is true?

options.text: Language impairment is the principal cause of the impaired daily functioning.
Most often behavioral symptoms, such as disinhibition and hyperorality, are the most prominent clinical manifestations at symptom onset.
Language symptoms are directly related to the frequency of word use.
The prototypical language variant of FTLD is caused by Pick's disease.
FTLD has sudden onset and rapid progression.

correct_answer.text: Language impairment is the principal cause of the impaired daily functioning.

correct_answers.text: Language impairment is the principal cause of the impaired daily functioning.

questions.explanation: A diagnosis of language-variant FTLD requires that the most prominent feature is difficulty with language, that the language impairment is the principal cause of impaired daily functioning, and that aphasia (rather than behavioral symptoms) is the most prominent deficit at symptom onset and for the initial stage of the disease. The language symptoms are unrelated to the frequency of word use. The prototypical behavioral variant of FTLD is caused by Pick’s disease and presents as personality change with progressive impairment of judgment, loss of social graces, disinhibition, stimulus boundedness, and a craving for sweets. FTLD has insidious onset and gradual progression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the categorization of aphasias in neurocognitive disorders is true?

options.text: In global aphasia, verbal fluency is impaired but repetition and naming are generally intact.
Anomic aphasia is uncommon in Alzheimer's disease.
Patients with Broca's aphasia can generally obey commands but have difficulty with repetition.
Unlike patients with Broca's aphasia, patients with Wernicke's aphasia have good comprehension.
In contrast to the naming difficulty in Wernicke's aphasia, the naming difficulty in Broca's aphasia is usually not helped by prompts.

correct_answer.text: Patients with Broca's aphasia can generally obey commands but have difficulty with repetition.

correct_answers.text: Patients with Broca's aphasia can generally obey commands but have difficulty with repetition.

questions.explanation: The categorization of aphasias is based on the language functions they impair. Global aphasia impairs all language functions and occurs in large left-hemisphere strokes. Anomic aphasia, by contrast, primarily affects word finding, may be related to lesions of the left angular or left posterior middle temporal gyrus, and is common in Alzheimer’s disease. Broca’s (anterior, nonfluent) aphasia impairs verbal fluency, repetition, and naming and results from lesions of the posterior inferior portion of the left (or dominant) frontal lobe. Patients with Broca’s aphasia generally understand what is said to them and can obey commands but have difficulty with repetition, reading aloud, and writing. Patients with Wernicke’s (posterior, fluent) aphasia have fluent (e.g., good flow of speech), paraphasic, and neologistic speech with poor comprehension, repetition, and naming. Although both Broca’s aphasia and Wernicke’s aphasia involve difficulty with naming, patients with Broca’s aphasia are usually aided by prompting, whereas patients with Wernicke’s aphasia are not.

questions.question_text: What aging-related change in the brain increases the risk of delirium induction from anticholinergic drugs?

options.text: Loss of dendritic arborization.
Loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert and septal nuclei.
Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra.
Expansion of the ventricular system.
Atrophy of cerebral cortex.

correct_answer.text: Loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert and septal nuclei.

correct_answers.text: Loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert and septal nuclei.

questions.explanation: Loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert and septal nuclei reduces cholinergic input to the forebrain and increases the likelihood of delirium from anticholinergic drugs such as bladder or gastrointestinal relaxants

questions.question_text: What aging-related change in the brain confers an increased sensitivity to the extrapyramidal effects of antipsychotic drugs?

options.text: Loss of dendritic arborization.
Loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert and septal nuclei.
Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra.
Expansion of the ventricular system.
Atrophy of cerebral cortex.

correct_answer.text: Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra.

correct_answers.text: Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra.

questions.explanation: Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra increases the sensitivity of dopamine D2 receptors and thus sensitivity to the extrapyramidal effects of antipsychotic agents.

questions.question_text: Which of the following clinical features would support a diagnosis of neurocognitive disorder over a diagnosis of depression?

options.text: Increased psychomotor activity.
Mood-congruent auditory hallucinations.
Frequent suicidal ideation.
Marked change in appetite.
Day/night confusion.

correct_answer.text: Day/night confusion.

correct_answers.text: Day/night confusion.

questions.explanation: In contrast to the typical presentation of depression, in neurocognitive disorders psychomotor activity is generally normal, visual hallucinations are more common, suicidal ideation is uncommon, and appetite is typically normal. Whereas patients with depression tend to report early awakening from sleep, patients with neurocognitive disorder often experience day/ night confusion, and many become transiently delirious toward the end of the day, a phenomenon known as sundowning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about management of delirium in an inpatient setting is true?

options.text: Pharmacological intervention is indicated even in mild delirium that does not cause sleep disturbance or interfere with medical treatment.
For delirium lasting longer than 7 days, providers should consider substance withdrawal as the likely cause.
Rooms should be kept dimly lit to avoid overstimulating the patient.
Mechanical restraints should be used in preference to sitters, because bedside companions often exacerbate confusion.
Patients should be frequently reoriented to time, place, and staff members.

correct_answer.text: Patients should be frequently reoriented to time, place, and staff members.

correct_answers.text: Patients should be frequently reoriented to time, place, and staff members.

questions.explanation: Substance withdrawal delirium should be presumed if symptoms begin 1–3 days after admission, and the patient’s substance use should be reviewed with family members when possible. Bedside companions (ideally, a well-liked family member) are preferable to and less dangerous than mechanical restraints. Rooms should be kept well lit to minimize misperceptions; a room with a window can assist with day/night orientation. Patients should be frequently reoriented to their surroundings—for example, clocks and calendars should be provided, and staff members should reintroduce themselves each time they visit. Mild delirium that does not cause sleep loss, interfere with medical treatment, or lead to extreme fear and discomfort does not require treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive abnormalities, if elicited on mental status examination of a patient with depression, would be most suggestive of an underlying comorbid neurocognitive disorder?

options.text: Impaired episodic memory.
Impaired attention.
Impaired orientation.
Reduced information-processing speed.
Impaired working memory.

correct_answer.text: Impaired orientation.

correct_answers.text: Impaired orientation.

questions.explanation: In an evaluation of a person with a cognitive complaint, depression must be considered as the cause or as an aggravating factor. Many depressed persons experience cognitive impairment, although the severity of their impairment does not correlate with the severity of their depressive symptoms. Persistent deficits in cognitive function often follow remission of depressive symptoms (Nebes et al. 2003), including deficits in working memory, speed of information processing, episodic memory, and attention. Impaired orientation, on the other hand, is a feature that, if present, would be more suggestive of underlying neurocognitive impairment

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes an advantage of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) over the Folstein Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)?

options.text: The MoCA takes less time to administer than the MMSE.
The MoCA has a larger scoring range than the MMSE.
The MoCA takes into account differences in education level.
The MoCA has greater sensitivity for detection of mild cognitive impairment.
The MoCA is more widely used and therefore more acceptable to the public.

correct_answer.text: The MoCA has greater sensitivity for detection of mild cognitive impairment.

correct_answers.text: The MoCA has greater sensitivity for detection of mild cognitive impairment.

questions.explanation: The MMSE (Folstein et al. 1975) is the most widely used brief screening tool for cognitive impairment (contra option E); it requires 10–15 minutes to administer and has a scoring range of 0–30. Like the MMSE, the MoCA (Nasreddine et al. 2005) requires about 15 minutes to administer and has a scoring range of 0–30 (therefore, options A and B are incorrect). Although it is true that the MMSE is confounded by premorbid intelligence and education (option C), the MoCA does not specifically address this problem. An advantage of the MoCA over the MMSE is that the former was designed to detect mild cognitive impairment (e.g., mild neurocognitive disorder), with a suggested cutoff of 27 points when used for that purpose; however, population-based norms developed for the MoCA suggest that a more appropriate cutoff score in the United States is 23 points (Rossetti et al. 2011).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cholinesterase inhibitors is true?

options.text: They may improve cognitive performance in individuals with neurocognitive disorders, but they do not slow the rate of cognitive decline.
Their use is absolutely contraindicated in individuals with bradycardia or bronchopulmonary disease.
They are effective only in major neurocognitive disorder due to probable Alzheimer's disease.
They are available only in oral formulations.
They are used as first-line monotherapy for patients with advanced major neurocognitive disorder.

correct_answer.text: They may improve cognitive performance in individuals with neurocognitive disorders, but they do not slow the rate of cognitive decline.

correct_answers.text: They may improve cognitive performance in individuals with neurocognitive disorders, but they do not slow the rate of cognitive decline.

questions.explanation: Cholinesterase inhibitors have been used with some success in patients with Alzheimer’s disease, Lewy body disease, and cognitive impairment associated with vascular disease (option C). This class of drugs, which also enhances cognition in persons without brain disease, raises baseline cognitive performance but does not slow the rate of decline (option A). All cholinesterase inhibitors are available in once-a-day preparations. Donepezil and galantamine are administered orally; rivastigmine is characteristically used as a patch (option D). A resting pulse below 50 and severe bronchopulmonary disease are relative contraindications (option B), but the treatment decision should be made on a case-by-case basis. Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine have different mechanisms of action; thus, combination therapy could, in theory, confer additional benefits (Tariot et al. 2004). This combination has become the preferred treatment in clinical practice for patients with moderate to severe Alzheimer’s disease (option E); however, recent evidence suggests that the addition of memantine to a cholinesterase inhibitor adds little to therapeutic efficacy (Howard et al. 2012)

questions.question_text: An 88-year-old man with major neurocognitive disorder secondary to probable Parkinson's disease begins to develop paranoia and agitation over the course of several months. Behavioral interventions are ineffective, and there is concern about caregiver burnout. Which of the following statements about pharmacological treatment of agitation with psychotic features during the course of a neurocognitive disorder is true?

options.text: Numerous antipsychotics have received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for treatment of behavioral disturbances in persons with neurocognitive disorders.
High doses of antipsychotics should be employed initially in order to control the behavior, and then tapered as tolerated with close monitoring for symptom recurrence.
Psychotropic medications that are helpful should be continued indefinitely.
An antipsychotic would be the first choice for treatment of agitation with psychotic features.

FDA warnings have been issued about increased cerebrovascular adverse events and increased mortality with use of typical antipsychotics but not with atypical antipsychotics in older dementia patients.

correct_answer.text: An antipsychotic would be the first choice for treatment of agitation with psychotic features.

correct_answers.text: An antipsychotic would be the first choice for treatment of agitation with psychotic features.

questions.explanation: No drug treatment has received FDA approval for any of the behavioral and emotional symptoms (except major depression and mania) that may arise during the course of a neurocognitive disorder. Because virtually all drugs used to treat behavioral disturbances in persons with neurocognitive disorders are administered off label, the general guideline for younger adults is to escalate dosage until the behavior is controlled or until untoward side effects occur. The psychopharmacological approach most commonly employed is that of Tariot (1999): 1. Use a drug with known efficacy in the symptom complex that most closely resembles the presenting symptoms. 2. Employ low dosages and escalate slowly, assessing both target symptoms and toxicity. 3. If a psychotropic medication is helpful, attempt to withdraw it at an appropriate time and monitor for recurrence of the problem. Using Tariot’s (1999) approach, antipsychotics would be the first choice for treatment of agitation with psychotic features. However, their therapeutic effects are often small and inconsistent. Their potential side effects (akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia, sedation, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, peripheral and central anticholinergic effects, postural hypotension, cardiac conduction defects, and falls) must be weighed against their potential benefits. There is no overall difference in efficacy between typical and atypical antipsychotic drugs, and little distinguishes them from each other except their sideeffect profiles. It is important to note that FDA warnings have been issued about increased cerebrovascular adverse events and increased mortality with both typical and atypical antipsychotics in elderly patients with dementia (U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2011).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the treatment of depression in individuals with neurocognitive disorders is true?

options.text: Depression cannot be diagnosed in persons with a neurocognitive disorder and therefore treatment is not indicated.
Serotonin reuptake agents have not been shown to have any benefit in persons with neurocognitive disorders.
Methylphenidate may be useful for reducing apathy and depression in Alzheimer's disease.
Stimulants are relatively safe agents with few side effects in persons with neurocognitive disorders.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the first-line treatment for depression in persons with neurocognitive disorders.

correct_answer.text: Methylphenidate may be useful for reducing apathy and depression in Alzheimer's disease.

correct_answers.text: Methylphenidate may be useful for reducing apathy and depression in Alzheimer's disease.

questions.explanation: Persons with any neurocognitive disorder may develop superimposed depression that should be treated in the same manner as persons without a neurocognitive disorder (option A). Serotonin reuptake agents can reduce irritability in depressed or nondepressed persons with neurocognitive disorders (Siddique et al. 2009) and may also increase alertness. Methylphenidate may be useful for reducing apathy and depression in Alzheimer’s disease (Padala et al. 2010), but no controlled clinical trials of stimulants have been performed in persons with neurocognitive disorders (option C). Stimulants can increase blood pressure and heart rate and lead to irritability, agitation, and psychosis, so caution is advised in using these agents (option D). Although electroconvulsive therapy can be used to treat severe depression in persons with any neurocognitive disorder, it is not first-line treatment, and cognitive side effects are more severe than for cognitively intact persons (option E).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most problematic limitation of high-dose vitamin E in the treatment of patients with neurocognitive disorders?

options.text: Association with increased cardiovascular adverse events.
Failure to significantly slow functional progression of the disease.
Potential to increase irritability, agitation, and psychosis in individuals with neurocognitive disorders.
Association with extrapyramidal side effects.
Association with postural hypotension and increased falls.

correct_answer.text: Association with increased cardiovascular adverse events.

correct_answers.text: Association with increased cardiovascular adverse events.

questions.explanation: Vitamin E dosages of 2,000 IU daily have been associated with a small but significant slowing of functional progression of Alzheimer’s disease but no improvement in cognition. This treatment, once in wide use, is now less frequently used because of an association of increased cardiovascular events with the use of high-dose vitamin E. Easy bleeding is a common side effect at this dosage but occurs infrequently at daily dosages of 800–1,000 IU.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the drug memantine is true?

options.text: Memantine is a reversible inhibitor of the enzyme acetylcholinesterase.
Memantine is typically dosed once daily.
Memantine is poorly absorbed and has a short half-life of 2.5 hours.
Memantine received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for early Alzheimer's disease.
Memantine may cause transient confusion or sedation during the titration phase, but generally has few adverse effects.

correct_answer.text: Memantine may cause transient confusion or sedation during the titration phase, but generally has few adverse effects.

correct_answers.text: Memantine may cause transient confusion or sedation during the titration phase, but generally has few adverse effects.

questions.explanation: The principal mechanism of action of memantine is believed to be the blockade of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)–type glutamate receptors, thereby improving synaptic transmission and/or preventing calcium release that may provide neuroprotection. It is not a cholinesterase inhibitor. Memantine is well absorbed and has a 70-hour or greater half-life, but is typically dosed twice daily because that was the dosage scheme used in efficacy studies. Memantine has received FDA approval for moderate to severe Alzheimer’s disease, and although widely used in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease, there are no convincing efficacy data to support this use. Memantine may cause transient confusion or sedation during the titration phase, but generally has few adverse effects

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the use of antiandrogens in controlling inappropriate sexual behavior is true?

options.text: There is no report of successful pharmacotherapy for inappropriate sexual behavior in individuals with cognitive impairment.
The antiandrogen medroxyprogesterone is effective in reducing sexual drive and sexually aggressive acts both in men who are cognitively intact and in men with brain injury.
The drug medroxyprogesterone is available only in an oral formulation.
Women with brain injury who are hypersexual are effectively treated with estrogen patches.
Medroxyprogesterone carries the risk of deep vein thrombosis.

correct_answer.text: The antiandrogen medroxyprogesterone is effective in reducing sexual drive and sexually aggressive acts both in men who are cognitively intact and in men with brain injury.

correct_answers.text: The antiandrogen medroxyprogesterone is effective in reducing sexual drive and sexually aggressive acts both in men who are cognitively intact and in men with brain injury.

questions.explanation: Antiandrogens are used to treat inappropriate sexual behavior or unwanted sexual approaches by persons with cognitive impairment (Guay 2008). The antiandrogen medroxyprogesterone is effective in reducing sexual drive and sexually aggressive acts both in men who are cognitively intact and in men with brain injury. The drug can be administered orally or intramuscularly, and side effects are minimal. Other drugs that have been used with some success include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, the luteinizing hormone–releasing hormone antagonist leuprolide, and estrogen patches. However, estrogen therapy carries the danger of deep vein thrombosis. There is no report of successful pharmacotherapy for hypersexual women with brain injury.

questions.question_text: What is the most preventable cause of neurocognitive disorders in young adults?

options.text: Substance abuse.
Traumatic brain injury due to motor vehicle accidents.
Human immunodeficiency virus infection.
Depression.
Nutritional deficiency.

correct_answer.text: Traumatic brain injury due to motor vehicle accidents.

correct_answers.text: Traumatic brain injury due to motor vehicle accidents.

questions.explanation: The most preventable cause of neurocognitive disorders in young adults is traumatic brain injury. The use of helmets for bicycle and motorcycle riders significantly reduces mortality and morbidity from head injuries, as do helmets in situations in which personnel are exposed to blast injury. Attention is also being paid to head injuries in sports (Khurana and Kaye 2012).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the psychopharmacological treatment of insomnia or disturbed sleep in individuals with a neurocognitive disorder is true?

options.text: Conventional hypnotics are generally avoided because of their tendency to increase irritability and agitation.
Conventional hypnotics are not recommended because they often exacerbate sleep-wake dysregulation.
Mood stabilizers should be first-line treatment for insomnia in persons with a neurocognitive disorder.
The rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder that is a frequent concomitant to Lewy body disease often responds to treatment with hypnotics such as trazodone.
The REM sleep behavior disorder that is a frequent concomitant to Lewy body disease often responds to anticholinesterase treatment.

correct_answer.text: The REM sleep behavior disorder that is a frequent concomitant to Lewy body disease often responds to anticholinesterase treatment.

correct_answers.text: The REM sleep behavior disorder that is a frequent concomitant to Lewy body disease often responds to anticholinesterase treatment.

questions.explanation: Although hypnotic drugs may be administered to the patient, they are generally prescribed so that caregivers can get adequate sleep. Conventional hypnotics are generally avoided because of their tendency to oversedate and to cause ataxia. Mood stabilizers are not indicated for treatment of insomnia. The REM sleep behavior disorder that accompanies Lewy body disease often responds to anticholinesterase treatment.
